body:
From the medialog spec's A5, regraded against source 2026-08-29: the transport already
supports non-interactive scoped credentials - serve()'s token map carries {actor: seed}
identities, and the key's reach is whatever grants it holds (write/register with --prefix,
federate per-container). What is missing is ERGONOMICS: minting one takes hand-editing serve
config, generating a seed, minting grants, and restarting the server.

Build `loam client mint <name>` : one verb that (1) generates a seed, stores it in the home
(0600, like user seeds), (2) mints the requested grants for its key (repeatable
--verb/--prefix pairs, --federate <container>), (3) adds a bearer token -> actor entry the
server honors, and (4) prints the bearer token once, with the artifact-exposure warning in its
own words (the token ships in client source; the scope is the safety). Pair with
`loam client revoke <name>` striking the grants and retiring the token.

The design decision to settle in P1: how a RUNNING server learns a new token - a tokens file
it re-reads (the credentials.json pattern), or a hot add on the handle. The staleness-warning
discipline (T103/T243) applies to whichever loses.

Acceptance criteria:
- (a) A minted client can read and write exactly its granted prefixes through the MCP door
  with the bearer token, and is refused outside them - two-sided. Verify:
  test/cli/client-mint.test.ts.
- (b) Revoke strikes on the next request, no restart, and a sibling client's standing
  survives. Verify: the same suite.
- (c) The mint prints the exposure warning and never prints the seed. Verify: the same suite
  at the CLI output level.
title: loam client mint: scoped non-interactive credentials in one verb
